records.source_title: HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10
records.author: mudamuda
records.text:
I've tried a separate PC with a different display port cable. Same issue observed after 30-40 minutes or so. Turning monitor on/off with the power button fixes it, as well as toggling HDR in the OS.
In SDR, I face no dimming issues at all. This is strictly limited to HDR.
The firmware I obtained is from the same page you've linked. When following the steps on the site and selecting the .inf after clicking "Have disk", I get this error:
"The folder you specified doesn't contain a compatible software driver for your device. If the folder contains a driver, make sure it is designed to work with Windows for x64-based systems."
I'm on Windows 11 and tried both the Windows 11 and Windows 10 files.

records.source_title: HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10
records.author: Hector_Lenovo
records.text:
Hi mudamuda!
Welcome to Lenovo Community, and thanks for describing the issue so clearly. I understand how frustrating it is when your Legion Pro 27Q-10 stays dim in HDR and only returns to normal after a power cycle.
Based on what you described, this does sound different from normal scene-based brightness behavior since the brightness recovers immediately after turning the monitor off and back on. As practical steps, please test with the same content after switching HDR off, try another certified display cable if available, and check whether the behavior is the same on another video source or system to help rule out signal-handling issues.
To help narrow this down, When the dimming happens, does it also occur if you switch the monitor to SDR (turn HDR off) for the same content, or only in HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) modes?
As for the update, are you perhaps referring to
this driver
? Could you share the exact error message you get when installing it?
Best regards,
Hector_Lenovo

records.source_title: HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10
records.author: mudamuda
records.text:
My Legion Pro 27Q-10 QD-OLED monitor has an issue in the HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) modes, where after 30-40 minutes of use the monitor dims permanently until I turn it off and on again. This is not because of ABL, if I pause a scene and turn it off/on in the same scene, the brightness immediately restores and the difference is obvious.
I tried installing the firmware using the steps provided on the site, but it fails the same as it does for everyone else using this monitor, per complaints on this forum and Reddit, since the provided files are not actual firmware updates but a Dolby Vision extension.
Please, Lenovo, upload the proper updated firmware files for this monitor.
This is on the Legion Pro 27Q-10 True Black 400 QD-OLED.

records.source_title: Lenovo - Legion Pro 27Q-10 Longterm review ("don't do it!"); incredible MOTION RESOLUTION.
records.author: @whitedragem
records.text:
Yes, different manufacturers can really go the distance for 'better products', and some- its like they never had 'real world testing'.

OLEDs at max brightness (a value that changes based on screen content/'average picture level'), can really etch a pixel into a users' brain.. 

eg this lenovo HDR monitor has a white text branding /logo that takes up part of the screen, but is introduced to screen over a 'few frames'; and its brightness value varies in stages as it renders this.

Shows 'nobody cares'; just a logo and we have to have it..
But for end users;?
Partner hates this OLED so much due to 'bedroom' time..
It lights the space like a lamp and the values vary "too much".
A system reboot (randomly required by techs like myself when doing stuff), will have this monitor "light house'" my sleeping space before settling to users preferences..

And it's sleep timeouts seem built to coincide with large signal handshaking times, this thing will happily do a few power cycles to rapify its product lifecycle to the trash can (it is, after all, 'Lenovo').

The irony that I replaced a 27"OLED with a 65" Samsung LCD.. (VA panel, 'quantum dot').
Samsungs quantum dot panel has such great backlight bleed control that blacks are black, and even though only 'single array' dimming; has exceptional screen brightness control and goes brighter and has better OLED range and pop.

Sure the Samung TV, on clearance, cost more.. (and is still junk from a manufacturer who builds for the scrap heap!)
But, menus and TV/monitor panel logic should be set in concrete by now; we have had decades to master this stuff.
My 35year+ ancient JVC TV cpuld rename inputs inside of twenty second.. (first time might take a minute to learn), that Samsung TV? Took minutes ad required help even though it has a graphical menu system, hi res, and lots of text.. just didnt care about 'end user' expereince..

Complex products?
Hardly..
Just not well thought out.
